subject: Chemistry
title: Discovery of Acids
description: A micro-lesson that makes Discovery of Acids usable.

hook.text: Alchemists discovered the three mineral acids—sulfuric, hydrochloric, and nitric—that made modern chemistry possible.

buildup.text: Sulfuric acid (oil of vitriol) was made by heating green vitriol (iron sulfate). Jabir described it in the 8th century.

discovery.text: Hydrochloric acid (spirit of salt) came from heating salt with vitriol. Nitric acid came from saltpeter and vitriol.

twist.text: These acids could dissolve metals, separate compounds, and create new substances—powers no previous chemical had.

climax.text: Without mineral acids, there would be no fertilizers, no explosives, no steel, no plastics. Industrial chemistry depends on them.

punchline.text: Three acids that dissolve metals and build industries. Alchemy's most useful legacy.

quiz.question: What were the three mineral acids discovered by alchemists?

details.summary: Islamic alchemists produced the first mineral acids: hydrochloric acid from salt and vitriol, nitric acid from saltpeter and vitriol, and aqua regia by mixing hydrochloric and nitric acids..
details.whyItMatters: Mineral acids are the foundation of modern chemical industry. Without their discovery by alchemists, processes from metal refining to pharmaceutical synthesis to fertilizer production would not exist.
takeaways: Hydrochloric, nitric, and sulfuric acids were first produced by alchemists
Aqua regia could dissolve gold, challenging the idea of gold's indestructibility
Mineral acids enabled chemical analysis and industrial chemistry

faq.question: Why was the discovery of mineral acids so transformative for chemistry?
faq.answer: Before mineral acids, alchemists had only weak organic acids like vinegar. Strong mineral acids could dissolve metals, decompose minerals, and drive reactions at room temperature that previously required extreme heat. They opened entirely new categories of chemical transformation.

faq.question: How did alchemists produce aqua regia and why was it so significant?
faq.answer: Aqua regia is a mixture of concentrated hydrochloric and nitric acids in a three-to-one ratio. It dissolves gold and platinum by forming soluble chloride complexes. Its ability to dissolve supposedly indestructible gold challenged fundamental assumptions about the nature of matter.
